translations.text: When they could no longer hide him, his mother took a reed basket, coated it with pitch, put the child in it, and placed it in a marsh by the riverbank.
His sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Would you like me to call a Hebrew nurse for you, so that she can nurse the child for you?”
Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Take this child and nurse him for me, and I will pay you your wages.” The woman took the child and nursed him.
God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
He said, “I will be with you, and this will be the sign to you that I sent you to bring my people out of Egypt: you will worship God on this mountain.”

The Lord said to Moses, “When you go and return to Egypt, see that you perform before Pharaoh all the signs that I have placed in your hands. But I will harden his heart, and he will not let the people go.”
Zipporah took a flint and circumcised her son’s foreskin. Falling at his feet, she said, “Look, the blood from my child’s circumcision has stopped.”
Moses told Aaron all the words of the Lord, who had sent him, and all the signs that he had commanded him to perform.
That day Pharaoh gave orders to the people’s taskmasters and their scribes, saying:
“Impose on them the same quota of bricks that they used to make each day. Do not reduce it at all, because they are idle. That is why they cry out and say, ‘Let us go and sacrifice to our God.’”
The taskmasters pressed them, saying, “Complete your work according to the daily quota, just as when straw was given to you.”
When they came out from Pharaoh’s presence, they met Moses and Aaron, who were coming toward them.
“Go in and speak to Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians, so that he will let the Israelites leave the land of the Egyptians.”
The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, who was of Phoenician descent. These are the clans of the sons of Simeon.
The sons of Uzziel were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Zithri.
“I will harden Pharaoh’s heart and multiply my signs and wonders in the land of the Egyptians.”
The wise men of Egypt did the same through their magic. Pharaoh’s heart hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had said.
Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of the Egyptians and brought up frogs. The frogs came up and covered the land of the Egyptians.
The wise men of Egypt did the same through their magic and brought up frogs in the land of the Egyptians.
“I will work wonders among the livestock of the Egyptians and among the livestock of Israel, and not a single one belonging to any of the Israelites will perish.”
God set a time, saying, “Tomorrow the Lord will do this thing upon the land.”
The Lord said to Moses, “Rise early in the morning, stand before Pharaoh, and say to him, ‘This is what the Lord, the God of the Hebrews, says: Let my people go, so that they may worship me.’”

The Lord said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward heaven, and there will be hail over all the land of the Egyptians—over people and livestock and over every plant in the fields of the land of the Egyptians.”
Pharaoh hurried to summon Moses and Aaron and said, “I have sinned before the Lord your God and against you.”
“Now forgive my offenses this once more, and plead with the Lord your God to remove these locusts from me.”
And the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he was unwilling to let them go.
And the people took their dough before it was leavened, with their lumps of dough wrapped in their cloths on their shoulders.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Consecrate to me every firstborn, the first offspring that opens any womb among the Israelites, whether human or animal, for it is mine.
You shall eat unleavened bread for seven days, and on the seventh day there shall be a feast to the Lord.
And the Egyptians pursued them and found them camped beside the sea—all Pharaoh’s horses and chariots, his horsemen and his army—in front of the resting place, opposite Baal-zephon.
And behold, I will harden the heart of Pharaoh and of all the Egyptians, and they will go in after them. And I will be glorified through Pharaoh and all his army, his chariots and his horses.
And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea and drove the sea back by the force of a south wind all night. He made the sea dry land, and the water was divided.
The nations heard and grew angry, and anguish seized the inhabitants of Canaan.
For Pharaoh’s horses went into the sea with his chariots and horsemen, and the Lord brought the waters of the sea upon them. But the Israelites walked on dry land in the midst of the sea.

Moses cried out to the Lord, and the Lord showed him a piece of wood. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There he established statutes and judgments for him, and there he tested him.
And behold, on the surface of the wilderness there was something small like coriander, white like frost on the ground.
And they gathered it morning by morning, each according to what he needed, and when the sun grew hot, it melted.
And Moses said, “Eat this today, for today is a Sabbath to the Lord. Today you will not find it in the field.”
And whenever Moses raised his hands, Israel prevailed, and whenever he lowered his hands, Amalek prevailed.
And Jethro, the priest of Midian, Moses’ father-in-law, heard everything that the Lord had done for Moses and for Israel, his people, and that the Lord had brought Israel out of Egypt.
And Jethro said, “Blessed is the Lord, who saved them from the hands of the Egyptians and from Pharaoh’s hand, for he delivered the people from under the hand of the Egyptians.”
In the third month after the Israelites came out of the land of the Egyptians, on that very day they came to the wilderness of Sinai.

And the Lord said to Moses, “Behold, I will come to you in a pillar of cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you and may believe you forever.” And Moses reported the people’s words to the Lord.
And God spoke to Moses and said, “Go down and warn the people, lest they approach to look at God and many of them perish.”
And I show mercy to a thousand generations of those who love me and who keep my commandments.
And Moses said to them, “Take courage, for God has come to you to test you, so that the fear of him may be in you, so that you do not sin.”
If someone strikes his male or female slave with a rod, and the slave dies at his hand, vengeance shall be exacted through judgment.
Let there be an oath by God between the two, that he has not dealt deceitfully in any way with what his neighbor entrusted to him. Then its owner shall accept it, and he shall not pay compensation.
You shall not withhold the produce of your threshing floor and your winepress. You shall give me the firstborn of your sons.
Keep everything that I have told you. Do not mention the names of foreign gods, and do not let them be heard from your mouth.

Celebrate the summer festival of the firstfruits of your produce, from the work you have cultivated in your field, and the festival at the end of the year, when you gather the produce of your work from the field.
The appearance of the Lord’s glory was like a blazing fire on the summit of the mountain, in the sight of the children of Israel.
Insert the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry the ark with them.
For the poles shall remain in the rings of the ark of the covenant, without being moved from it.
Make two pillars for the corners of the tabernacle on its rear side.
Put the poles through the rings. The poles shall be on both sides of the altar, for carrying it.
On the other side, the curtains shall be fifteen cubits high, with three pillars and three bases.
They shall take gold, blue and purple material, spun scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
With the skilled workmanship of gem engravers, engrave the two stones as a seal is engraved, according to the names of the children of Israel. Make them stamped and engraved in gold.
Make two gold rings and place them on the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, on the underside, facing one another at the joining, and its [?] above the woven work of the ephod.
For Aaron’s sons, make tunics, sashes, and headdresses, for honor and glory.

Aaron and his sons shall wear it when they enter the tent of testimony or when they approach the holy altar to minister. They must not bring sin upon themselves, lest they die. This is an everlasting ordinance for him and his descendants after him.
Take them from their hands and offer them on the altar of burnt offerings as a pleasing aroma before the Lord, for it is an offering to the Lord.
I will meet the children of Israel there, and I will be sanctified by my glory.
Overlay it with pure gold—its grating, its sides all around, and its horns—and make a gold molding around it.
Do not make incense for yourselves according to that preparation, for it shall be holy to the Lord for you.
Keep the Sabbaths, for the Sabbath is holy to the Lord and to you. Whoever profanes it shall be put to death. Whoever does any work on it shall be cut off from among his people.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said, “Go down from here quickly, for your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt, have acted lawlessly.”

They quickly turned aside from the way you commanded them. They made themselves a cast calf, bowed down to it, sacrificed to it, and said, “These are your gods, Israel, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.”
Moses said to Aaron, “What did this people do to you, that you brought this terrible sin upon them?”
The next day, Moses said to the people, “You have committed this great sin. But now I will go up to God, so that I may make atonement for your sins.”
The children of Israel stripped off their ornaments and their robes at Mount Horeb.
The Lord said, “Here is a place before me, and you shall stand on the rock.”
Celebrate the Festival of Weeks for me at the beginning of the wheat harvest, and the festival of gathering the crops in the middle of the year.
All those skilled in heart among the workers made the tabernacle with ten curtains of finely spun linen, blue, purple, and double-dyed scarlet, with cherubim worked into the fabric.
He made fifty gold clasps and joined the curtains to one another with the clasps, so that the tabernacle became one whole.
He made bars of rot-resistant wood, five for one upright on one side of the tabernacle.
He made a border a handbreadth wide all around it, and made gold moldings all around its border.
They inserted the poles into the rings on the sides of the table to carry the table with them. He made it entirely of boards.
They made two gold rings and placed them on the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, on its lower side, at its front, by the upper join of the woven ephod.
They made woven linen tunics for Aaron and his sons.

All the work on the tabernacle, the tent of testimony, was completed. The Israelites did everything just as the Lord had commanded Moses. From the gold left over from the offerings, they made utensils with which to serve before the Lord.
You shall place the ark of testimony there and screen the ark with the curtain.
You shall anoint the courtyard all around and hang the curtain at the entrance to the courtyard.
He placed the lamps on it before the Lord, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
